year_display.zh: 铭牌 1976 年 5 月 4 日随卫星发射；NASA 说明

edition.en: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, LAGEOS mission pages, ‘Message to the Future’. The page’s wording is kept as published, including one sentence that is missing its verb. The same ‘Message to the Future’ text appears in NASA’s 1976 LAGEOS press kit (Release 76-67).
edition.zh: NASA 戈达德航天中心 LAGEOS 任务网页“致未来的信息”。文字照原样保留，包括其中一句缺了动词的句子。同一篇“致未来的信息”见于 NASA 1976 年的 LAGEOS 新闻资料包（新闻稿 76-67）。

source.name: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, LAGEOS

basis.en: Text written and published by NASA (it first appeared in NASA’s 1976 LAGEOS press kit and refers to Carl Sagan, the plaque’s designer, in the third person), and so a US federal government work, which is not subject to copyright (17 U.S.C. § 105).
basis.zh: 由 NASA 撰写并发布的文字（最早见于 NASA 1976 年的 LAGEOS 新闻资料包，文中以第三人称提到铭牌设计者卡尔·萨根），属于美国联邦政府作品，不受版权保护（《美国法典》第 17 编第 105 条）。

note.en: LAGEOS is a brass and aluminium ball covered in mirrors, placed in a very stable orbit in 1976 so that lasers on the ground could measure how the continents move. Sealed inside it is a plaque designed by Carl Sagan for whoever lives on Earth when it falls back, millions of years from now. Unlike most messages on this shelf it is addressed to our own distant descendants, and it tells the time with the very thing the satellite was built to measure.
note.zh: LAGEOS 是一个铝壳黄铜芯、表面布满反射镜的球，1976 年被送入一条非常稳定的轨道，好让地面的激光测量大陆怎样移动。它里面封存着一块卡尔·萨根设计的铭牌，留给几百万年后它落回地球时住在地球上的人。和这个书架上的大多数信息不同，它是写给我们自己遥远的后代的；而它用来计时的，正是这颗卫星被造出来要测量的东西。

pick.en: I would keep this one because its clock is honest. It does not trust any calendar to survive; it trusts the continents, and it rounds its numbers on purpose so as not to claim more precision than anyone had. ‘A little greeting card from the remote past’ is also the most modest sentence on the shelf, and modesty seems right when writing to people that far away.
pick.zh: 我会留下它，是因为它的时钟是诚实的。它不相信任何历法能流传下去，它相信的是大陆；它还故意把数字取整，不肯冒称比任何人实际掌握的更精确。“一张来自远古的小小贺卡”也是这个书架上最谦逊的一句话；给那么遥远的人写信，谦逊似乎是对的。

excerpt.orig: Whoever is inhabiting Earth in that distant epoch may appreciate a little greeting card from the remote past.
excerpt.en: Whoever is inhabiting Earth in that distant epoch may appreciate a little greeting card from the remote past.
excerpt.zh: 在那个遥远的时代住在地球上的无论是谁，也许会喜欢这张来自远古的小小贺卡。

marginalia.at: The close fit of South America into West Africa one of the first hints
marginalia.en: This is the sentence that lacks its verb, kept as published; read ‘was one of the first hints’. The observation is old: mapmakers remarked on the matching coastlines as early as the sixteenth century.
marginalia.zh: 这就是那句缺了动词的句子，照原样保留；读作“是最早的线索之一”。这个观察由来已久：早在十六世纪，就有制图家注意到两岸海岸线的吻合。

marginalia.at: Many of the other changes in the map of the Earth shown are little more than guesses.
marginalia.en: A plaque built to last for millions of years says plainly that most of its picture of the future is guesswork. Official writing seldom admits the limits of its forecasts so calmly.
marginalia.zh: 一块要保存几百万年的铭牌，坦白地说它对未来的描绘大多是猜测。官方文字很少这样坦然地承认自己预测的局限。

marginalia.at: Thus, the prime objective of LAGEOS and the method of telling time of the spacecraft's plaque are identical.
marginalia.en: The satellite measures continental drift, and the plaque uses continental drift as its clock. The message and the instrument are one design, so whoever can read the clock already knows what the satellite was for.
marginalia.zh: 卫星测量大陆漂移，铭牌就用大陆漂移来计时。信息和仪器是同一个设计，所以能读懂这只时钟的人，也就已经知道这颗卫星是做什么用的。
